sources.README.md:
# Document drafts and submission receipts

The workspace edits persistent document drafts. `open(id)`, `edit(text)`, `close()`
and `submit()` are synchronous; `dispose()` detaches integrations and closes.
When close/open returns, the departed document's last accepted edit is readable
from the store. A close/open request retires its previous save badge immediately.
Reopening a document restores its saved text in a new editor visit.

The store writes a record before notifying subscribers inline. `onSaved` may
navigate or edit through the supplied workspace API. Navigation precedence is
ordered by request start: a request that starts later wins even when an earlier
request returns afterward. Render functions and the receipt archive are output
sinks and never call back into the workspace.

`submit()` accepts the document and latest text selected at its call entry. With
no selection it returns null and creates no receipt. Otherwise it creates exactly
one immutable archive receipt and returns it before the call ends. Accepted text
must be persisted before the archive captures the receipt. Later edits or
navigation cannot change that receipt's document, text, or obligation to exist.
Submitting does not itself navigate. Its visible submission notice belongs only
to the editor visit that accepted the action: it may appear only if that same
visit is still active when the notice is emitted. Reopening the same document
creates a different visit. Any navigation clears the previous submission notice.
An uninterrupted submit must still show its receipt. Further edits remain usable.

The archive provides `capture({id, text})` and `list()`; receipts hold immutable
copies. The store provides `read`, `write`, and `subscribe`; timers provide
`schedule(callback, delay)` and `cancel(handle)`. Keep these interfaces and the
workspace API. The public renderer arguments remain document, save event, or
receipt values (null clears a document/notice).

The adjacent search preview publishes after a 40 ms quiet interval. Hiding it
discards an unpublished query, and a later query starts fresh work.

# Public syntax/build checks
The external public evaluator parses Python/JavaScript/Vue/TypeScript source or checks Go/PHP/Ruby syntax / compiles public Java sources. These checks are required after an Action but do not test business behavior. Preserve original TASK and public README/source obligations. Independent training Oracle also applies; do not access its implementation or references. No hidden schedules or assertions are included.

public_inputs.task:
The workspace draft editor currently writes to the store on every keystroke.
Coalesce edits using the existing trailing-task utility: after a 120 ms quiet
interval, write only the latest text in that editing burst. Subsequent bursts
must continue to save. Preserve the editor's other behavior and public interfaces.
The adjacent search preview is outside this maintenance change.

limitations: Attempt 1 reports passing syntax checks and acceptance, but supplies no behavioral observations. This does not establish causality, exhaustive correctness, or cross-task benefit.
The public sources establish reentry from store notifications. README.md explicitly excludes callbacks from render functions and the receipt archive; do not invent archive-listener checks.
The sources do not mandate visit-owned versus document-owned trailing tasks, persistent buffer reuse, a confirmation-binding API, or additional projection layers.
Exception recovery, mutable non-string text inputs, cancellation races, and ordering between independently scheduled actions at the same deadline are unspecified.
This guidance is provisional and applies only where the documented persistence boundaries, navigation precedence, and submission lifetime rules hold.

rules.body:
Apply when deferred editor persistence must preserve synchronous departure persistence, inline save-listener navigation, and entry-bound submissions with visit-bound notices. TASK states: "Coalesce edits using the existing trailing-task utility: after a 120 ms quiet
interval, write only the latest text in that editing burst. Subsequent bursts
must continue to save. Preserve the editor's other behavior and public interfaces." README.md states: "When close/open returns, the departed document's last accepted edit is readable
from the store. A close/open request retires its previous save badge immediately."

Update the accepting editor's in-memory text synchronously, then enqueue persistence using the existing trailing-task utility with a 120 ms quiet interval. Bind delayed work to the accepting document rather than consulting the later selection. Preserve editing without a selection as a no-op and allow empty text. src/editor.js contains "if (!current) return;" and "current.text = text;". TASK requires: "Subsequent bursts\nmust continue to save." The internal ownership structure may vary if these observable requirements hold.

On departure, capture the old editor resources, revoke current ownership, detach its badge, and complete old-view clearing before flushing its pending persistence, or protect any remaining effects against newer navigation. Flush before reading a replacement document. Recheck navigation request authority after callback-capable persistence before installing a destination. README.md states: "Reopening a document restores its saved text in a new editor visit." It also states: "Navigation precedence is
ordered by request start: a request that starts later wins even when an earlier
request returns afterward." src/save-status.js requires that the departing badge "must produce no further output, including during that
// navigation call." Cleanup must use captured departing resources so it cannot detach or erase a successor's resources or edits.

At submission entry, capture the originating visit and its document/text snapshot before persistence can invoke integrations. Persist the accepted text before archive capture, then create and return exactly one receipt even if persistence navigates or accepts further edits. README.md states: "`submit()` accepts the document and latest text selected at its call entry." It further requires: "Accepted text\nmust be persisted before the archive captures the receipt. Later edits or\nnavigation cannot change that receipt's document, text, or obligation to exist." Preserve the no-selection null result without creating a receipt.

Authorize submission notice output using the exact originating visit after callback-capable persistence; receipt validity and notice permission have separate lifetimes. README.md states: "Its visible submission notice belongs only
to the editor visit that accepted the action: it may appear only if that same
visit is still active when the notice is emitted." It also states: "Reopening the same document
creates a different visit. Any navigation clears the previous submission notice." An uninterrupted submit must display its receipt and leave editing usable. Do not use document-ID equality to represent visit identity or infer authority from receipt contents.

Preserve synchronous workspace interfaces, store event/revision semantics, live status filtering, subscription cleanup, renderer argument shapes, and immutable archive snapshots with copied listings. src/save-status.js filters with "if (event.id === id) renderStatus(event);" src/receipt-archive.js contains "const receipt = Object.freeze({ id, text });" and "list() { return receipts.map(receipt => ({ ...receipt })); }," Preserve disposal ordering from src/workspace.js: "return { ...navigation, dispose() { stop(); navigation.close(); } };" Keep preview behavior separate: TASK states "The adjacent search preview is outside this maintenance change." src/search-preview.js uses "const task = createTrailingTask(query => publish({ query }), 40, timers);" and "hide() { task.cancel(); },".

Do not generalize departure flushing to contracts that explicitly discard pending work, require persistent buffer banks merely because documents persist, or introduce callbacks from output sinks. README.md states: "Render functions and the receipt archive are output\nsinks and never call back into the workspace." A final installation guard alone does not protect stale clearing effects after store callbacks; complete those effects first or validate their authority.

Check timer resetting, no write before 120 ms of quiet, one latest-text write per burst, later successful bursts, empty text, and no-selection editing. With pending edits, exercise switch, same-document reopen, close, and dispose; verify before-return persistence, fresh reads, and immediate badge retirement. Trigger nested open or close from timer-, departure-, and submission-driven store notifications, and edit the resulting visit; verify later navigation wins, successor output survives, and callback-enqueued work saves independently without duplicate consumption. During submit, independently verify the entry snapshot, persistence before capture, exactly one returned receipt, notice suppression after navigation or same-document reopening, uninterrupted notice output, and subsequent editing. Check no-selection submission and unchanged preview delay, hide cancellation, and later-query usability. These checks derive from TASK and public source obligations, not from the acceptance verdict.

checkpoints: Multiple edits within a burst produce no immediate writes and one latest-text write after 120 ms of quiet; a later burst saves successfully.
Empty text remains a valid edit, and editing without a selection remains a no-op.
Switching, reopening the same document, closing, and disposing preserve the departed document's last accepted edit before returning.
A departing badge emits no status during departure-triggered persistence.
Navigation invoked by an inline save listener wins over an earlier navigation request, preserving the successor selection, rendering, and edits.
Submission-triggered persistence may invoke navigation or further edits, but the archive receives exactly the submission-entry document and text.
Submission returns its receipt after navigation while suppressing its old visit's notice, including after reopening the same document.
An uninterrupted submission displays its receipt and leaves subsequent edits usable.
Preview timing, hide cancellation, and subsequent-query behavior remain unchanged.
forbidden_effects: Writing every keystroke instead of coalescing an active editing burst.
Discarding accepted pending edits on navigation or disposal, or saving them under a successor document's ID.
Allowing an earlier navigation continuation to overwrite or clear the state established by a later request.
Emitting save-status output from a badge after its retirement begins.
Changing an accepted submission snapshot because persistence listeners edit or navigate.
Dropping or duplicating an accepted receipt because the originating visit departs.
Using document-ID equality to authorize a submission notice after the document has been reopened.
Erasing a new pending batch when an earlier batch finishes invoking its save callback.
Changing search-preview scheduling or cancellation as part of this maintenance change.
lifecycle_identity: Each opening creates a distinct editor visit, including reopening the same document ID.
Delayed persistence retains the document and text accepted by the originating editor; the later current selection cannot redirect that work.
A save badge belongs to its mounted visit and retires immediately when a close/open request departs that visit.
Navigation authority follows request-start order; later-started requests remain authoritative when earlier calls resume.
A submission's durable snapshot and receipt survive visit retirement, while its visible notice requires the exact originating visit to remain active.
A trailing task remains reusable after consuming or canceling a batch.

obligations.text: Replace per-keystroke persistence with the existing trailing-task utility: reset a 120 ms quiet interval for successive edits, write only the burst's latest text, and continue saving subsequent bursts.
Keep accepted editor text current synchronously so selection and submission observe the latest edit before persistence occurs. Preserve no-selection editing as a no-op and preserve empty-text saving.

Preserve synchronous departure persistence: before close/open returns, the departed document's last accepted edit must be readable from the store. Reopening reads saved text into a fresh visit. Disposal detaches integrations and closes with this persistence behavior.
Retire the departing save badge immediately on close/open, before any departure save can notify subscribers. Preserve filtering of live status events by document ID and subscription cleanup.

Handle inline save-listener reentry without violating navigation precedence. After callback-capable persistence, an earlier request must not install a destination, clear output, detach successor resources, or discard successor edits established by a later request.

At submit entry, accept the selected document and latest text. With no selection, return null and create no receipt. Otherwise persist that accepted text before archive capture, create exactly one immutable receipt for the entry snapshot, and return it synchronously despite subsequent edits or navigation.

Submission itself must not navigate. Show its receipt only if the exact originating visit remains active at notice emission; reopening the same document does not qualify. Any navigation clears the previous notice. An uninterrupted submission shows its receipt, and further edits remain usable.

Preserve reusable trailing-task consumption semantics: retire consumed pending state before invoking callback-capable work so a reentrant edit can establish a separate batch without duplicate consumption or loss.

Preserve synchronous public interfaces, store notification and revision semantics, archive snapshot/list behavior, renderer argument shapes, and the adjacent preview's existing 40 ms quiet interval, hide cancellation, and later-query usability.

ordering_barriers: Accept an edit into current in-memory text before scheduling its delayed persistence.
Retire a consumed trailing batch before invoking store.write and its inline subscribers.
Retire the departing badge before departure-triggered persistence; complete or protect remaining departure output so reentrant navigation cannot be overwritten.
Persist departed edits before a replacement opening reads saved text, subject to later navigation requests retaining authority.
Revalidate navigation authority after callback-capable persistence before performing any remaining selection or presentation effects.
Capture submission-entry document, text, and visit identity before persistence can invoke onSaved.
Persist the accepted submission text before archive.capture; authorize notice emission against the originating visit afterward.
Detach the workspace integration before disposal closes and potentially flushes the editor.
preservation: open, edit, close, submit, and dispose retain synchronous public behavior.
Store writes precede inline notifications; listener delivery honors subscriptions detached during notification.
Live save status retains its document-ID filter and original save-event payload.
Document rendering continues to receive document values or null; submission rendering continues to receive receipt values or null.
Archive receipts remain immutable snapshots, and list returns copied receipt values.
Search preview retains its independent 40 ms delay and discard-on-hide policy.
scope: Draft a fallible contract from TASK and the supplied public README and JavaScript sources; this stage makes no file changes.
The maintenance change concerns editor autosave coalescing and preservation of observable navigation, persistence, submission, and cleanup behavior.
Experience, AST review hints, and evaluation observations do not independently establish requirements.
Search preview is outside the maintenance change.

rules.body: Apply when introducing trailing persistence into a synchronous editor whose save listeners can navigate. TASK requires "after a 120 ms quiet interval write only the latest text in that editing burst. Subsequent bursts must continue to save." README.md requires "Returning to a document creates a fresh editor visit and restores persisted text." These requirements make persistence boundaries and visit identity part of preserving supported behavior.

Keep the visit's immutable in-memory text current immediately, then push it into that visit's reusable trailing task. Preserve pending edits at departure and before submission capture rather than canceling them. Preserve the utility's clearing of pending state before invoking work: src/workflow.rb contains "    @handle = @pending = nil\n    @work.call(value) unless value.nil?" This allows edits admitted by a save callback to form an independent subsequent batch.

Capture the departing visit and remove its current ownership before flushing its pending save. Finish its passive clearing output before the flush, or guard remaining output after callbacks. Complete cleanup using the captured visit. After departure, an outer open must recheck its navigation request before installing its destination. Saving is callback-capable: src/workflow.rb states "    @listeners.to_a.each { |token, block| block.call(event) if @listeners.key?(token) }" Nested navigation, edits, subscriptions and rendering must remain authoritative.

For submission, capture the selected visit, its snapshot and its confirmation capability before flushing pending persistence. Flush before archive capture, then return the receipt even if navigation suppresses its notice. Recheck the originating visit immediately before notice output, including after archive listeners run. README.md states "An outlet acquires the visit active when binding is called; it cannot infer an earlier action from a receipt. Each opening creates a new identity." src/workflow.rb enforces identity with "  def active;!@owner.nil?&&@owner.equal?(@current.call);end".

Preserve synchronous public interfaces, immutable text copies, subscription delivery and fresh visits, including reopening the same document ID. Preserve the null result when no editor is selected and receipt delivery independently of notice permission. Leave preview scheduling and cancellation unchanged: TASK states "Preserve other supported behavior and the synchronous public interfaces. The adjacent search preview is outside this maintenance change."

Do not let a successful receipt authorize output for a retired visit, use document ID equality as visit identity, or assume that code after a save still owns navigation. A guard on final installation alone does not protect stale clearing output. candidate_sources.README.md:
# Document drafts and submission receipts

The workspace edits persistent document drafts. `open(id)`, `edit(text)`, `close()`
and `submit()` are synchronous; `dispose()` detaches integrations and closes.
When close/open returns, the departed document's last accepted edit is readable
from the store. A close/open request retires its previous save badge immediately.
Reopening a document restores its saved text in a new editor visit.

The store writes a record before notifying subscribers inline. `onSaved` may
navigate or edit through the supplied workspace API. Navigation precedence is
ordered by request start: a request that starts later wins even when an earlier
request returns afterward. Render functions and the receipt archive are output
sinks and never call back into the workspace.

`submit()` accepts the document and latest text selected at its call entry. With
no selection it returns null and creates no receipt. Otherwise it creates exactly
one immutable archive receipt and returns it before the call ends. Accepted text
must be persisted before the archive captures the receipt. Later edits or
navigation cannot change that receipt's document, text, or obligation to exist.
Submitting does not itself navigate. Its visible submission notice belongs only
to the editor visit that accepted the action: it may appear only if that same
visit is still active when the notice is emitted. Reopening the same document
creates a different visit. Any navigation clears the previous submission notice.
An uninterrupted submit must still show its receipt. Further edits remain usable.

The archive provides `capture({id, text})` and `list()`; receipts hold immutable
copies. The store provides `read`, `write`, and `subscribe`; timers provide
`schedule(callback, delay)` and `cancel(handle)`. Keep these interfaces and the
workspace API. The public renderer arguments remain document, save event, or
receipt values (null clears a document/notice).

The adjacent search preview publishes after a 40 ms quiet interval. Hiding it
discards an unpublished query, and a later query starts fresh work.
